question.text: The range of the function $f(x)=\sqrt{3 x^2-4 x+5}$ is

solution.text:
$f(x)$ is defined if $3 x^2-4 x+5 \geq 0$
$\Rightarrow 3\left[x^2-\frac{4}{3} x+\frac{5}{3}\right] \geq 0 \Rightarrow 3\left[\left(x-\frac{2}{3}\right)^2+\frac{11}{9}\right] \geq 0$
Which is true for all real $x \therefore$ Domain of $f(x)=$ $(-\infty, \infty)$
Let $y=\sqrt{3 x^2-4 x+5}$
$\Rightarrow y^2=3 x^2-4 x+5$ i.e. $3 x^2-4 x+\left(5-y^2\right)=0$
For $x$ to be real , $16-12\left(5-y^2\right) \geq 0 \Rightarrow y \geq \sqrt{\frac{11}{3}}$
$\therefore \quad$ Range of $y=\left[\sqrt{\frac{11}{3}}, \infty\right)$
